newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia SIDANKO Oil assumes units' executive duties.
newsitem.headline: Russia SIDANKO Oil assumes units' executive duties.

text.p: Subsidiaries of Russian oil group SIDANKO are to transfer to the parent company their executive and administrative functions in a further consolidation of the group, SIDANKO said on Wednesday.

"It is expected that the new management system will be approved by the annual meetings of all oil production and refining enterprises of the Company in May-June this year, and by most oil marketing organisations in 1998," it said in a statement.

SIDANKO (Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya) is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating units are Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz and the Angarsk refinery.

"The new management system will make it possible to increase the company's efficiency as a single operation and is an important step in the preparations for the issuing a single share for the SIDANKO group," the statement said.

Similar steps have already been taken by some other Russian oil majors such as LUKoil and YUKOS. YUKOS in turn has transferred most management functions to controlling shareholder Bank Menatep's industrial holding company Rosprom.
SIDANKO is mostly owned by Interros-Oil, which is associated with Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) and Bank MFK.
